cards.title: Lightning leaps metal
cards.text: A shock that lands on a machine, turret or golem jumps on to the nearest other metal thing.
cards.why: The Foundry starts rewarding lightning heroes, and a fight there looks different: sparks running down a line of bots.
cards.pick: Yes. Your own turrets are spared, so it never punishes the Engineer.

cards.title: Wet machines short out
cards.text: A soaked machine hit by lightning stalls for a moment, in a shower of sparks.
cards.why: Water heroes (the new Water Mage) and storm heroes start working together. Machines already take more shock when wet, so it's one small step on.
cards.pick: Yes, about half a second, at most once every few seconds per machine.

cards.title: Machines: repair only
cards.text: Healing spells, potions and songs do nothing to turrets, totems and golems; only repairs fix them.
cards.why: It makes the Engineer's wrench (and repair drones) the only way to keep a construct standing, so builders matter. It costs healers a little in parties with turrets.
cards.pick: Yes, for both sides: enemy repair drones keep their job, enemy healers can't mend machines.

cards.title: Deaf to songs
cards.text: Machines, golems and slimes ignore every song, shout and howl, both their side's and yours.
cards.why: No lullaby putting a turret to sleep, no war cry speeding up a golem. The rule is already in the tag system, waiting for kinds.

cards.title: Fliers really fly
cards.text: Bats, spirits and angels are in the air for good: puddles, fire and slams miss them, shots don't.
cards.why: Ranged heroes get a job, and flying rooms play differently. Big change: those enemies get harder for melee parties, so some abilities would need to bring them down.
cards.pick: Yes, with a few heroes able to ground them (nets, the bolas, a gust).

cards.title: Sharp cuts, blunt dazes
cards.text: Every sharp blow builds a little bleeding, every blunt one a little stagger.
cards.why: Weapons would feel different even at the same damage: a sword party bleeds things down, a hammer party keeps them reeling.
cards.pick: Maybe. A lot of small numbers to tune; I'd try it after the resistance calls settle.

cards.title: A muzzle for loud ones
cards.text: An ability that hushes one enemy at a time: no howl, song, fire breath or bite for a few seconds.
cards.why: Silence now only stops the mouth, so it needs a way in for heroes. A hero picking off the Choir Sprite's song or a wolf pack's howl is a clear, readable job.
cards.pick: Yes, as a Monk ability (a vow of silence laid on a foe).

cards.title: A beast-tamer's calm
cards.text: Soothe an animal: wolves, boars and bats stop fighting for a while, or for good if they're weak.
cards.why: Uses the beast tag, and gives the Wildwood and the Warren an answer that isn't damage.
cards.pick: Yes, as a Druid tier or a new hero.

cards.title: Burning plants spread
cards.text: Ents, sproutlings and the hay bale, once burning, set fire to the ground they walk on.
cards.why: Fire heroes get a big payoff in the Wildwood, but burning enemies would also spread fire under your own feet.
cards.pick: Maybe. The Wildwood is the first dungeon, so I'd keep it to the Elder Ent's fight for now.

cards.title: A magic hunter
cards.text: A new enemy that shrugs off half of every spell's hit but still burns, freezes and gets soaked.
cards.why: Your own example. Mage parties have to lean on their effects instead of raw spell damage; weapon heroes get a target they're best at.
cards.pick: Yes, an elite in the Gilded Spire or the Crypt.
